The Bohr model arranges electrons in discrete energy levels or shells, and the number of these shells corresponds to the period (row) in the periodic table.  
For example, hydrogen and helium are in row 1 and have 1 shell, lithium to neon are in row 2 and have 2 shells, and so on.  
This is determined by the principal quantum number \( n \), which matches the row number.
